key_insight: The paper introduces accelerated second-order Lagrange-multiplier optimization schemes with pseudo-energy dissipation that are designed to converge stably to stationary points in non-convex problems.
engineering_relevance: These methods can improve training robustness and solution quality for scientific machine learning and PDE-constrained modeling, including PINNs and DeepONets.
method: Linear LM-based second-order flow for unconstrained non-convex optimization.
Linear LM-based variable and operator splitting method.
Relaxed and adaptive variants to prevent multiplier degeneration and auto-tune time step size.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive numerical tests on function optimization and PDE benchmarks, showing improved escape from local minima, high accuracy, and strong robustness to the initial learning rate.
watch_item: The methods add algorithmic complexity and may require careful tuning of splitting, relaxation, and step-size update rules in practical implementations.
paper_title: Several Accelerated and Stable Pseudo-Energy-Dissipative Lagrange Multiplier Methods based on Second-order Flow and Variable Splitting
